chunks: And from him from Muhammad ibn Isma'il who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the shade for the person in ihram from the harm of rain or sun, so he said, 'I see that he should ransom himself with a sheep which he slaughters at Mina.' The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'And whoever argues while he is in ihram truthfully once or twice, there is no expiation upon him and he seeks forgiveness from Allah, Exalted and Glorious. And if he argues three times truthfully, then whatever is more than that, upon him is the blood of a sheep. And if he argues once falsely, upon him is the blood of a sheep. And if he argues twice falsely, upon him is the blood of a cow. And if he argues three times falsely, and whatever is more, upon him is the blood of a camel.'
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for arguing while in the state of ihram during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the graduated financial expiation (dam) for disputes during Hajj, distinguishing between truthful and false arguments to reflect the severity of the breach. It establishes a proportional penalty structure where truthful disputes incur no penalty for one or two instances, while false arguments escalate from a sheep to a cow and finally a camel, demonstrating the juristic precision in balancing intent with ritual violation.
